newsitem.title: USA: ISSUER FOCUS-DC GO sale seen drawing good interest.
newsitem.headline: ISSUER FOCUS-DC GO sale seen drawing good interest.

text.p: The District of Columbia's $234 million competitive general obligation bond deal slated for pricing Wednesday has drawn solid investor interest and active syndicate bidding for the issue, dealers and analysts said.
The $234 million deal is slated to fund $150 million in capital projects and $84 million to refund current debt. It is structured as serial bonds starting in 1998 and going out to 2026.
A total of six syndicates will bid on the deal, according to market sources, up from two on the last District of Coulumbia deal, a $171 million offering in October 1996.

"From what we've heard, there's quite a bit of interest in the District of Columbia. It's still relatively cheap because the rating (Ba2/single-B/BB-plus) is what it is, so it's seen as a good place to get a pretty good rate without being too risky," said one analyst.

The last deal, in October 1996, came at 110 basis points over Municipal Market Data 30-year AAA GO curve and was all sold at pricing. Dealers said the current deal would likely launch at a tighter spread, especially if it comes with the insurance the last deal lacked.

"If it comes with insurance, it will come well through 105. If it's unenhanced, I think it will come through that (spread level) simply because every account is looking for yield," said one syndicate source.
One insurer is "looking closely" at insuring the deal, according to an official there, noting that District of Columbia is considered an improving credit.

Besides Merrill Lynch & Co., which won the last deal, and Lehman Brothers, the only other competing bid on that issue, the current offering will draw bids from groups led by PaineWebber Inc., Bear Stearns & Co, Prudential Securities Inc and Goldman Sachs & Co., market sources said.
"It kind of surprised me when I saw the number of bidders," said another syndicate official.
